topic: Authoritative Roadmap for Public Developer Preview Release and Progressive Evolution toward Two Paradigms: (2a) The Full-Stack Builder and (2b) The Autonomous Emerging Organisation

inputs.claude: Paradigm 2a (The Full-Stack Builder) and Paradigm 2b (The Autonomous Organisation) are not competing architectures; they are sequential phases of organizational emergence. A fully autonomous organisation (2b) cannot exist stably without first mastering the atomic unit of collaboration: a biological agent directing specialized synthetic roles through explicit policy, verified evidence, and unambiguous handoffs (2a)...
inputs.agy: The greatest risk to Synlynk's public debut is not lack of capability, but cognitive overload and installation friction. Over 5 months of rapid evolution, Synlynk has accumulated immense power, but also operational complexity. To prove Paradigm 2a, Synlynk must deliver an undeniable Time-to-Wow under 15 minutes...
inputs.codex: From a systems engineering perspective, Synlynk cannot achieve widespread adoption or enterprise credibility until its execution environment is completely hermetic. The divergence between Agy's release reporting and Claude's audit highlighted a critical vulnerability: Synlynk has operated in an editable install inside worktrees paradigm...
inputs.grok: Paradigm 2b posits that an autonomous organization emerges from a set of policy directives and goals, leveraging any available resources (biological, AI models, tools, infra). This requires a dynamic capability engine rather than hardcoded agent pipelines...

synthesis: The panel unanimously converges on a cohesive, two-phase strategy that directly validates Paradigms 2a and 2b: Strategic Progression (2a -> 2b), Immediate Stability Prerequisite (hermetic packaging, zero test failures, clean root), and Frictionless Onboarding UX.
decision: Adopt the Authoritative Master Roadmap for Synlynk: Phase 1: The Full-Stack Builder (v0.29.0 Developer Preview Launch) and Phase 2: The Autonomous Organisation (v1.0.0+ Enterprise & Swarm Expansion).
